role.altitude: The dermatologist keeps examining, diagnosing, treating, operating and counselling; typing notes, letters, medication lists and questionnaire answers shrinks.
skills_to_grow: Correcting scribe drafts quickly and carefully
role.ambitious_version: A dermatologist whose time goes to patients, not typing.

tasks.short: Examine lesions with the dermatoscope and talk with the patient, compare with earlier images, decide diagnosis and treatment, perform excisions and biopsies, write the consultation note, request pathology and answer patient questions to diagnose and treat pigmented lesions such as nevi or melanoma.

steps.what: Dermatologist examines pigmented lesions such as nevi or melanoma with the dermatoscope and talks with the patient
Dermatologist compares dermoscopy images with earlier images
Dermatologist decides diagnosis and treatment
Dermatologist performs excisions and biopsies
Dermatologist writes the consultation note

loop.input: The recorded consultation, with the patient's consent, and the structured data in the record.
loop.output: A draft consultation note in the record template.
loop.check: The dermatologist reads and corrects every note before it is saved; a monthly sample audit looks for omissions.
loop.stop: The dermatologist writes the note when the recording is incomplete or the patient declines recording.

steps.what: Dermatologist writes the pathology request in the record
Dermatologist answers patient questions by message

tasks.design: With the patient's consent, a certified scribe drafts the consultation note from the recorded consultation, and the dermatologist corrects every note before it is saved. The pathology request fills from the validated note. Examining, comparing images, diagnosis, treatment, surgery and patient questions stay with the dermatologist. No model reads the lesion.
tasks.previous_blocker: Notes and requests were typed after each consultation.
tasks.enabler_now: Certified ambient scribes that write into the record after validation.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing the ugly duckling among dozens of moles.

reach.learn: Whether requests carry the clinical question.

evidence.claim: In a peer-reviewed study of 236,153 scribe notes, self-estimated time per note fell from 6.69 to 4.72 minutes; three of seven authors were from the vendor.
A clinical scribe and coding tool carries MDR class IIa.
Ambient recording captures staff performance and needs works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: diagnosing and treating pigmented lesions; ordering diagnostic tests (task 17084) is a sibling task.
s5 is priced at 75 and s6 at 70 because every text is corrected; patients consent to recording and the works council consents.
Examination, image comparison, decisions, surgery and questions keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of patients who consent to recording.
research_questions: Does note time per consultation fall?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few patients consent; high: most consent.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Check screening history, counsel patients on screenings, sun protection, skin cancer awareness and self-examination, give information leaflets, document counselling and answer follow-up questions.

steps.what: Dermatologist checks the patient's screening history in the record
Dermatologist counsels patients on dermatologic screenings, sun protection and skin self-examinations
Dermatologist selects and prints information leaflets
Dermatologist documents counselling in the record

loop.input: The recorded consultation, with the patient's consent, and the structured data in the record.
loop.output: A draft consultation note in the record template.
loop.check: The dermatologist reads and corrects every note before it is saved; a monthly sample audit looks for omissions.
loop.stop: The dermatologist writes the note when the recording is incomplete or the patient declines recording.

steps.what: Dermatologist answers follow-up questions by message

loop.input: The patient's question and vetted, guideline-based patient texts.
loop.output: A draft reply citing the text it draws on.
loop.check: Each reply cites its paragraph and the dermatologist reads and signs it before sending.
loop.stop: Questions about the patient's own diagnosis go to the dermatologist unanswered.
loop.why_not_simpler: Patients ask in their own words.

tasks.design: Leaflets from vetted, guideline-based patient texts are linked in the patient portal from a short list, instead of being selected and printed. Counselling is noted by the scribe draft that the dermatologist corrects. Follow-up replies start from drafts that cite the vetted text, and the dermatologist reads and signs each. Counselling stays with the dermatologist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Leaflets were printed and notes and replies typed one by one.
tasks.enabler_now: Vetted patient texts, scribes and reply drafting with citations.
tasks.still_hard: Patients who do not use the portal.
tasks.human_edge: Persuading a sun-seeking patient to change habits.

reach.learn: Whether information is easy to find later.

evidence.claim: A patient information site is guideline-based and written with professional bodies and a patients' federation.
In a peer-reviewed study of 236,153 scribe notes, self-estimated time per note fell from 6.69 to 4.72 minutes; three of seven authors were from the vendor.
Ambient recording captures staff performance and needs works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: counselling on prevention; diagnosing and treating skin conditions (task 17095) is in this set and a separate task.
s3 keeps half; s4 is priced at 75; s5 at 80 because every reply is read and signed.
unknowns: Number of follow-up questions per week.
research_questions: Do patients find information without asking?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: patients without the portal; high: most patients on the portal.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Examine patients and discuss symptoms, decide diagnosis and treatment, perform treatments, write the consultation note, write prescriptions, draft, check and send the letter to the GP and answer patient questions to diagnose and treat skin conditions such as acne, psoriasis or skin cancer.

steps.what: Dermatologist examines patients and discusses symptoms of skin conditions such as acne, psoriasis or skin cancer
Dermatologist decides diagnosis and treatment plan
Dermatologist performs treatments such as cryotherapy and excisions
Dermatologist writes the consultation note

loop.input: The recorded consultation, with the patient's consent, and the structured data in the record.
loop.output: A draft consultation note in the record template.
loop.check: The dermatologist reads and corrects every note before it is saved; a monthly sample audit looks for omissions.
loop.stop: The dermatologist writes the note when the recording is incomplete or the patient declines recording.

steps.what: Dermatologist writes prescriptions in the prescribing system
Dermatologist writes the letter to the GP
Dermatologist checks and signs the final GP letter
Dermatologist sends the signed letter to the GP
Dermatologist answers patient questions by message

approvals.approved_version: The GP letter exactly as checked and signed by the dermatologist in s7, sent to the patient's own GP; any change needs a new signature.

tasks.design: With consent, a certified scribe drafts the consultation note, which the dermatologist corrects. The GP letter fills from the validated note and prescription, and the dermatologist checks and signs it before it is sent. Examination, diagnosis, treatment, prescribing and patient questions stay with the dermatologist; medication checks run in the prescribing system as today.
tasks.previous_blocker: Notes and letters were typed after each consultation.
tasks.enabler_now: Certified scribes and letters filled from validated notes.
tasks.still_hard: Complex patients whose letters need careful wording.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing a treatment the patient will keep using.

evidence.claim: In a peer-reviewed study of 236,153 scribe notes, self-estimated time per note fell from 6.69 to 4.72 minutes; three of seven authors were from the vendor.
A clinical scribe and coding tool carries MDR class IIa.
Ambient recording captures staff performance and needs works council consent.
A prescription comes from a named practitioner; drafting tools do not prescribe.

assumptions: Boundary: diagnosing and treating skin conditions; prescribing hormonal and topical agents (task 17089) is a sibling task, but writing prescriptions at the visit stays here at full time.
s4 is priced at 75 and s6 at 60 because every text is corrected.
Patients consent to recording and the works council consents.
research_questions: Do GP letters go out sooner?

already_counted.description: Dermatologist corrects drafted notes and letters.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few recorded consultations; high: most recorded.

tasks.short: Let patients fill a pre-visit questionnaire, review referral letters and earlier records, take the history in conversation, retype medication and allergies, copy questionnaire answers, write the history in the record and request missing records to record patients' health histories.

steps.what: Patient fills the pre-visit skin history questionnaire in the portal
Dermatologist reviews referral letters and earlier records
Dermatologist takes the health history in conversation with the patient
Dermatologist retypes medication and allergies from the referral letter into the record
Dermatologist copies questionnaire answers into the record
Dermatologist records patients' health histories in the record

loop.input: The recorded consultation, with the patient's consent, and the structured data in the record.
loop.output: A draft consultation note in the record template.
loop.check: The dermatologist reads and corrects every note before it is saved; a monthly sample audit looks for omissions.
loop.stop: The dermatologist writes the note when the recording is incomplete or the patient declines recording.

steps.what: Dermatologist requests missing records from the GP by mail

tasks.design: Medication and allergies arrive by integration from the patient's medication overview, instead of being retyped from referral letters. The patient's pre-visit questionnaire answers flow into the record, instead of being copied. With consent, the scribe drafts the history from the conversation, and the dermatologist corrects it before it is saved. Reviewing letters, taking the history and requesting records stay with the dermatologist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Medication, answers and history were typed by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Medication integration, portal questionnaires feeding the record and certified scribes.
tasks.human_edge: Asking the question that uncovers the real trigger.

evidence.claim: In a peer-reviewed study of 236,153 scribe notes, self-estimated time per note fell from 6.69 to 4.72 minutes; three of seven authors were from the vendor.
A clinical scribe and coding tool carries MDR class IIa.
Ambient recording captures staff performance and needs works council consent.
Health data are special category; expect a DPIA.

assumptions: Boundary: recording health histories; recommending diagnostic tests (task 17085) is a sibling task.
Input contract for s4: about 60% of patients have a medication overview available by integration; s4 is priced at that share.
s5 keeps 30 for checks; s6 is priced at 70 because every history is corrected.
Patients' questionnaire time is shown in s1 and replaces part of their verbal history.
unknowns: Share of patients completing the questionnaire.
research_questions: Do medication errors in the record fall?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few questionnaires and overviews; high: most patients complete both.
